conceptual assets.information: The software-programmable enable state controls whether the TWI block runs, clears its FIFOs, drives the clock-generator enable, and participates in interrupt generation.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because an unchecked bus write changes ctrl.enable at line 136. Availability is at risk because ctrl.enable clears both FIFOs at line 168, gates clock generation at lines 252-265, and drives clkgen_en_o at line 270.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could issue a bus write that clears the enable state, disables clock generation, and clears pending TWI data.

conceptual assets.information: The prescaler and clock-divider settings determine the rate of the generated TWI timing phases, on which serial transfers depend.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because bus writes load ctrl.prsc and ctrl.cdiv at lines 137-138 without an RTL authorization check. Availability is at risk because these settings select clkgen_i and determine counter rollover and tick generation at lines 257-264.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could write an extreme or incorrect prescaler or divider value to alter TWI timing or prevent useful transfer progress.

conceptual assets.concept: TWI transfer command and acknowledge control
conceptual assets.information: The command and acknowledge-control fields in a transmit FIFO word select the TWI operation and protocol response that the engine performs.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because bus_req_i.data is written into the transmit command path at line 198 and command and acknowledge information is loaded into engine.state and engine.sreg at lines 327-329. Availability is at risk because disabling the block clears the transmit FIFO at line 168 and fifo.tx_re only removes a command when the engine is idle, data is available, and a timing tick occurs at line 199.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could write altered command or acknowledge fields, causing the engine to perform the wrong TWI operation or preventing the intended operation from being served.

conceptual assets.information: The transmit byte supplied by software is serialized onto the TWI SDA data line as part of a commanded transfer.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is at risk because the supplied byte can be exposed on twi_sda_o through the serialization path at lines 374 and 406. Integrity is at risk because bus_req_i.data supplies the transmit FIFO at line 198 and the engine loads the transmitted bits at line 327. Availability is at risk because ctrl.enable clears the transmit FIFO at line 168 and the transmit-read condition at line 199 can withhold a queued byte.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter or clear a queued transmit byte, or observe the resulting SDA waveform, causing incorrect or exposed TWI data.

conceptual assets.information: The byte sampled from the TWI SDA input is assembled during a transfer and returned to software through the receive-data bus read.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is at risk because received data is exposed in bus_rsp_o.data at line 156. Integrity is at risk because twi_sda_i enters the sampling path at line 408 and sampled data is incorporated into engine.sreg at line 378 before the receive read. Availability is at risk because disabling the block clears the receive FIFO at line 168 and receive data is only written when engine.done asserts at line 229.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could drive or interfere with SDA samples, clear the receive path, or otherwise cause incorrect or unavailable received data to be returned.

conceptual assets.information: The interrupt notification indicates that TWI is enabled, the transmit FIFO is empty, and the engine is idle, allowing software to service or start further transfers.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because irq_o is generated from enable, transmit availability, and engine state at line 239, so altered control or status can create a false notification. Availability is at risk because suppressing the notification can prevent software from servicing the empty transmit path and can halt subsequent transfers.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could suppress or falsely assert irq_o, causing software to miss a required transfer service event or act on an incorrect readiness indication.

considered, not kept.reason: The clock-stretch setting only affects the serial clock timing path at line 296, and twi_scl_i and twi_scl_o are serial-link clock lines excluded by the clocks and resets rule.
clkgen_i only enables the counter and tick progression at lines 257-264, while clk_gen.cnt, clk_gen.tick, and phase signals only pace transfers and are excluded by the pacing-pulse rule.

IO_TWI_FIFO and log2_fifo_size_c only fix implementation size at build time, as shown at lines 20 and 64, so no runtime element can change or withhold them.
